batch_node.name: Core dimension vocabulary v0.1.0
batch_node.description: Dimension nodes for the dimension keys core itself stamps (req-grid-dimension-core-vocabulary). Dimensions are declared, never created on demand (aws-build Q48a).

node.name: tap.meta
node.description: What kind of grid record a node is, for records that describe the grid itself rather than observe the world. Core stamps it on every Dimension node (value `dimension`) and on the keystone (value `keystone`). Bounded by use, open as declared: core owns the values.

node.name: tap.graph
node.description: Which graph a node belongs to. Core's web layer stamps `web` on its own models and edges (tap_web/dimensions.py), so presentation records partition from observed ones.

node.name: tap_cares
node.description: Which part of the collection machinery (tap_cares) a record belongs to: `collector`, `collection_job`, `schedule`, `schedule_fire`. Core stamps it on tap_cares' own models. Not a dotted name; declared under its current name and renamed later if wanted (a rename is one field update on this node).

batch_node.name: Core dimension vocabulary v0.2.0: time
batch_node.description: The `tap.time` dimension and a description node for each of its four values (req-grid-dimension-core-vocabulary, req-grid-entity-event-time). A batch of its own with its own fixed id, so a grid that already imported the first batch still receives these.

node.name: tap.time
node.description: What a row's event time means: the kind of time its `event_start` states (req-grid-entity-event-time). The grid stamps it on every node and edge that has an event time, derived from the type's declaration (`src: derived`); no writer may set it. Bounded: each value has a description node named `time.<value>`. The start and end themselves are the typed columns `event_start` and `event_end`, never a value of this dimension.

node.name: tap.time.occurred
node.description: The `occurred` value of the `tap.time` dimension: the event time is when the thing happened in the world, as its source states it (a log entry, a run, a sign-in). No counterpart in a formal code list: ISO 19115-1 `CI_DateTypeCode`, Dublin Core and DataCite have no term for an event occurring. Security and event schemas carry the idea as their default time field (OCSF `time`, the normalized event occurrence time; Elastic Common Schema `@timestamp`; CloudEvents `time`; W3C PROV-O `atTime`).

node.name: tap.time.created
node.description: The `created` value of the `tap.time` dimension: the event time is when the thing came to exist, as its source states it (a repository, an instance, an account). Counterparts: ISO 19115-1 `CI_DateTypeCode` `creation`; Dublin Core `created` (ISO 15836-2); DataCite `Created`; STIX `created`; OCSF `created_time`.

node.name: tap.time.first_seen
node.description: The `first_seen` value of the `tap.time` dimension: the event time is when a source first observed the thing, where the source states that and not when the thing itself began (a finding, an indicator). No counterpart in a formal code list. Security schemas carry it as a field name: STIX `first_seen` and `first_observed`, OCSF `first_seen_time`.

node.name: tap.time.published
node.description: The `published` value of the `tap.time` dimension: the event time is when the thing was issued or made public by its author (an advisory, a release, a report). Counterparts: ISO 19115-1 `CI_DateTypeCode` `publication`; Dublin Core `issued` (ISO 15836-2); DataCite `Issued`; STIX and OSV `published`; CVE `datePublished`.
